summary: A file system with no room left refuses a write with ENOSPC and gives the space back when the file goes; the program is tests/diskfull.c

cases.behavior: a file written on the test image's root until a write is refused is refused with ENOSPC after bytes were written, and once it is removed a block can be written again

execution.privileges: root, which writes the root directory
execution.cleanup: it removes its file on every path but a failed unlink; the root is the boot's own

assertions.checks: the file on the root is created, bytes are written to it, and a write within 32 MiB is refused
the refusal is ENOSPC, not EIO or another error
once the file is removed, a new file takes a block of 4 KiB written whole

native.reason: the probe fills the root file system of the machine it runs on; tests/native/probes.cases runs it in a private root of 16 MiB
